schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE R (A INT, B INT);
q1: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
counterexample: INSERT INTO R (A, B) VALUES (1, 10), (2, NULL);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 counts the total number of rows in table R, while Q2 counts the number of non-NULL values in column B of table R.
counterexample_dsp: A table R with at least one NULL value in column B will trigger a difference in the results of Q1 and Q2.
q1_validation_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS A FROM R AS X
q2_validation_sql: SELECT COUNT(Y.B) FROM R AS Y
